findings.cross_file_justification: The gate is read in agy_headless_adapter.complete()/health_check()/validate_config() with no project_root, so the trust anchor is whatever .loa.config.yaml the cwd walk finds at dispatch time.
findings.description: The opt-in that decides whether the redacted diff is placed on the agy CLI's argv (readable by every local account via /proc/<pid>/cmdline) is read from the cwd-walked project config on every call. The adapter's own docstring states the caller's cwd is the reviewed tree. In a PR-review flow, that tree's .loa.config.yaml is contributor-controlled, so a PR that adds `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` can enable the route the operator believed was off, exposing the prompt on a shared host and spawning `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions --sandbox`. The docstring's stated goal ('the argv prompt is only ever exposed by an operator's deliberate choice') is not met when the config layer is the tree under review.
findings.failure_mode: A reviewed branch flips the key; the next review dispatch opts into the argv-exposed Google CLI voice without operator action.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the gate against the operator's framework root (the root that owns .claude/adapters), or require the key to also be present in a non-tree source (system defaults or an operator-only file). At minimum, read it once at process start from cheval's own resolved root rather than per-call from cwd, and log the path the decision was read from.

findings.description: build_headless_argv exposes a `prompt` parameter that places untrusted prompt text directly on argv after `-p`, with no `--` separator. Neither the adapter nor the probe uses it (both pass None and stream the prompt on stdin), so it is a dead surface that re-opens the argv exposure cycle-126 closed and lets a prompt beginning with `-` be parsed as a CLI flag if any future caller passes it.
findings.failure_mode: A future caller passes the prompt positionally; a crafted diff starting with `--` is interpreted as claude CLI flags, and the prompt becomes visible in ps/cmdline.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `prompt` parameter (stdin is the only transport), or if it must stay, insert `--` before it and document that it must never carry review content.

findings.description: The opt-in rationale says 'No environment override — a planner is never talked into the agy voice by ambient env', yet once opted in the binary that receives the full prompt on argv is chosen by the ambient AGY_HEADLESS_BIN variable (and CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN for the claude route). Ambient env can redirect the dispatch to any executable without touching config.
findings.failure_mode: An inherited environment variable points the opted-in dispatch at an arbitrary binary which receives the redacted diff and runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the *_BIN override as a test seam: honour it only when a config flag permits it, or require an absolute path and log the resolved binary at WARN once per process alongside the existing argv-exposure warning.

findings.description: resolve_effort validates the catalog and extra rungs through _valid_effort but returns the caller rung (`args.effort`) unchecked, relying on argparse `choices` elsewhere. The value reaches the claude CLI argv via build_headless_argv and the HTTP effort field. The chokepoint's own contract is 'one chokepoint, four rungs' but one rung bypasses the validator.
findings.failure_mode: If the argparse definition ever loses its choices restriction, or a programmatic caller passes a Namespace, an arbitrary string lands on `--effort` and in MODELINV telemetry.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `explicit` through `_valid_effort` as well and fail with INVALID_CONFIG on mismatch, so the chokepoint does not depend on the argparse definition staying in sync.

metadata.status_note: no findings met the BLOCKING/ADVISORY bar — not an approval of unreviewed surface
